text.en: Raju heard that the Sun makes its energy by fusing hydrogen. "Nuclear energy powers the stars," said his teacher.

Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from certain elements, discovered by Becquerel in pitchblende, an ore of uranium. Natural radioactivity occurs on its own and artificial or induced radioactivity makes even light elements radioactive. The disintegrating nucleus is the parent and the one produced is the daughter. The curie, 3.7 x 10^10 disintegrations per second, and the becquerel are the units.
Alpha, beta and gamma are three kinds of radiations and each decay follows displacement laws. Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus like uranium-235 into smaller nuclei with a large release of energy and a chain reaction; the minimum mass needed is the critical mass, and the atom bomb uses an uncontrolled chain. Nuclear fusion is the joining of light nuclei to form a heavier one, as in the Sun and stars, and the hydrogen bomb.
Radioisotopes are used in agriculture, medicine and industry, but radiation is dangerous, so safety measures and permitted limits are followed. A nuclear reactor produces controlled fission energy, and India has several nuclear power plants.

problem.en: Name the energy source of the Sun.

prompt.en: A friend says Fission joins two light nuclei. How will you reply?

points.en: The curie is a unit of radioactivity.
